scope: Proposition 3.2 (Reversible chart transport) of the manuscript “Nontrivial Markov Type Forces Superreflexivity” (preprints/Nontrivial-Markov-Type-Forces-Superreflexivity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 327 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5df09ebb518ff529), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Λ be a finite ordered set, and let Ts : Ds → Rs be order-preserving bijections between its subsets, indexed by a nonempty finite set S with a fixed- point-free involution s 7→ s−1 and Ts−1 = T−1 s . For every ϵ > 0, there are an integer B and a finite stationary reversible marked chain on charts C : Λ → {1, . . . , B} whose successive edge letters are independent and uniform in S. At every stationary step (C, s, C′), C′ (a) = C(Ts(a)) (a ∈ Ds) holds simultaneously with probability at least 1 − ϵ.
